doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: How Lettuce got its name and early touring hardships
summary: Lettuce meant let us use your house; shared hotel rooms, exposure gigs.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I want to take you back to the thing you said about being packed into a van and sleeping on the floor. I mean that sounds like my rock & roll days. I mean some things never change, right?

Yeah, that’s how the band Lettuce started too. It’s like the word “lettuce” was like let us use your house, or like let us use your food, let us use your instruments. Because we were like let us sleep on your floor. So really yes, we played these crazy gigs, and then afterwards you’d think like where is the hotel but you’re like okay, I’ll get that corner over there. It happens. It’s all part of the struggle.
Now when you go to play a gig, like you said you went to New Orleans, I assume that —

Yeah. It’s a bed. There’s always a bed now. That’s a good thing. That’s always a plus. But even with my band, when we first started getting around I mean there was four of us and my manager, we’d all share one room. It would be two people in a bed and the manager on the floor. But after a while you get tired, definitely. When you’re younger you know like it’s fun just to be able to play out.
Yeah. There’s sort of the adventure factor.
“This is a good exposure gig for you.”
Yeah. How many times did I hear that.
Really. I have to laugh because Carmen Caramanica around here said, “You know you can’t eat exposure.”
Yeah. I know. You can’t eat exposure.
